subject: Private Offer: passback %, invoice path, and partner margin reconciliation
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie@cloudworks.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer questions + channel passback mechanics

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CloudWorks is excited about Redwood for inference workloads. Our procurement lead asked for a couple of clarifications before we move to a formal private offer: 

- How will the reseller/channel passback be represented on the invoice (list price vs. net credit)?
- We need to validate the margin our distributor will receive; can you confirm the typical % passback you support for Azure private offers and whether that is configurable per-deal?
- Any preferred format for evidence we should include for their finance team (invoice path diagram, line-item mapping)?

Attaching a short worksheet with our expected SKU mix. Can your team review and propose a passback approach we can include in the PO?

Best,
Sophie Lang
Head of Procurement
CloudWorks

[Attachment: cloudworks_privoffer_requirements.xlsx (XLSX)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private offer questions + channel passback mechanics

Ben / Irene — forwarding CloudWorks' workbook and questions. They want: (1) how passback shows on invoice, (2) typical passback % for Azure PO and whether configurable, and (3) evidence format for their finance team.

Quick asks:
- Ben: can you run numbers on a 12-month commit using the attached SKU mix and propose a recommended passback percentage and list/net invoice language? Include a conservative cushion we should keep for margins if we allow a 5–7% reseller uplift.
- Irene: any red flags on the invoice path (privacy/audit logs) or KMS/credit handling we should call out to the customer?

Goal: give Sophie a short spec + sample invoice line mapping they can attach to their PO. Target reply EOD today if possible — Sophie wants to move to legal next week.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Forwarded attachment: cloudworks_privoffer_requirements.xlsx]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer questions + channel passback mechanics

Grace / Irene — reviewed the workbook. Quick summary and recommendation: 

1) Invoice path: recommend we show Greenwood (CloudWorks' distributor) as a line-item credit on the invoice:
   - Line A: Redwood list price (SKU x qty)
   - Line B: Partner passback credit (negative line) referencing distributor ID and PO number
   - Net: Invoice total after passback
   This preserves gross-to-net traceability for their auditors and avoids embedding the credit into unit price.

2) Passback %: based on the SKU mix and usage profile, propose a configurable 6% passback to the channel with a hard floor of 4% (Redwood retains a 2% cushion for underwriting/billing variance). Rationale: 6% gives the distributor margin while keeping deal economics within our target. If CloudWorks asks for 8–10%, we should require a higher commit or shorter term.

3) Cushion and holdback: recommend a month-90 true-up where passbacks are reconciled against actual usage; any overpayment is recouped on the next invoice. Add a clause for retroactive adjustment if usage patterns deviate more than 20%.

4) Evidence pack: include:
   - PNG diagram of invoice path (invoice_path_diagram.png)
   - Line-item mapping table (we can export CSV)
   - Sample credit memo template

Irene — anything else from compliance side? If not, I can draft the one-pager and sample invoice snippet to send back to Sophie.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: current_invoice_path_diagram.png]

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie@cloudworks.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer questions + channel passback mechanics

Ben / Grace — +1 to Ben's plan. A couple of compliance notes to include in the one-pager for CloudWorks: 

- Billing auditability: ensure the credit line includes a reference to the underlying usage invoice(s) (invoice numbers or invoice period). That helps their auditors reconcile credits to charges.
- Data segregation: for Azure private offers, confirm we will route billing metadata through their distributor marketplace account ID (we can set this in the PO). Add this callout so CloudWorks sees the mapping between billing account and distributor ID.
- KMS & logs: if CloudWorks requires proof that invoice data did not include customer usage payloads, we can provide billing metadata logs (reddacted) for audit. This is standard but may require an NDA amendment depending on their legal.

Grace — I drafted a 1-page response and attached both the invoice diagram and a short mapping table. Sophie — cc'ing you so you have the exact language we propose. If you're comfortable, we can send the one-pager and a sample credit memo for procurement to attach to the PO.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
